Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Medford OR
510 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026

.Updated AVIATION Discussion...

&&

.AVIATION...25/00Z TAFs...A front will gradually move onshore this 
evening and inland overnight into Friday morning. Gusty south to 
southwest winds will continue ahead of this front, with a secondary 
uptick in winds expected between 09z-15z Friday morning. Winds will 
be strongest along the coast and over the marine waters, and low 
level wind shear will be a concern north of Cape Blanco this evening 
through around 09z before stronger winds aloft surface late tonight. 

VFR conditions prevail across the region, but expect conditions to 
lower to MVFR along the coast as moderate precipitation moves 
onshore between 01z-03z. There is a slight chance of thunderstorms 
along the coast as this front moves inland. Ceilings lower inland to 
the Cascades as well, but should remain VFR. The front will wash out 
as it moves inland, so expect VFR conditions to prevail east of the 
Cascades and across northern California. Showers will follow behind 
the front through Friday morning, mainly along the coast and north 
of the Rogue-Umpqua Divide. Otherwise, clouds will gradually 
dissipate late Friday morning into the afternoon. /BR-y

&&

.PREV DISCUSSION... /Issued 301 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026/ 

KEY MESSAGES...

* Gusty winds are expected along the coast and in the high 
  Cascades later tonight.

* Wetting rain is expected west of the Cascades with a low chance
  of rain by Friday morning.

* Temperatures cooler than normal Friday into the weekend.

* Low impact weather continues into the weekend with some areas of
  frost and freezing temperatures Friday night.

DISCUSSION...

Radar echos are starting to show up off the coast this afternoon
as warm moist air moves in ahead of cold front. That cold front
should swing through the southern Oregon coast later tonight into
Friday morning with wetting rainfall along the coast and over
locations west of the Cascades. Rainfall will generally be 0.15 
to 0.4 inches with significantly lower totals east of the 
Cascades. Northern California will also miss out of the rain as 
the moisture and lifting mechanisms are farther to the north.

Main impacts from this event will be some gusty winds in the
Cascades and along the coast. The extreme forecast index(EFI) is
pointing out unusually high wind speed and wind gust values off
our coastline in the Pacific. However, nothing really stands out
over land. We're expecting some gusts to 45 mph near North Bend 
with the frontal passage. Those stronger wind gusts should also
hit the higher Cascades and exposed areas around Crater Lake and
Diamond Lake.

Eventually, the cold front will push into southern Oregon later 
tonight around 10 to 11 pm and move eastwards overnight.
Temperatures will cool rapidly overnight and trend about 10
degrees cooler for Friday night. There is some risk of frost and
freezing temperatures in northern California near Tennant and
Tulelake area Friday night. We're holding off on any products
right now, although it is something to watch for. Right now the
NBM has a 80-90% chance of reaching 32F around Tennant and Bray in
central Siskiyou County.

Later in the day, the trough axis will shift eastwards by Friday 
afternoon and we'll see isolated showers over southern Oregon by 
Friday afternoon. Conditions gradually trend drier into the day as
high pressure slowly builds.

By this weekend, things will quiet down with temperatures much 
cooler than normal as highs push into lower 70's and upper 60's, 
which is roughly 10 degrees cooler than normal for late September.
Heading into next week, zonal flow is more likely with a warm 
front pushing into southern Oregon and northern California.
Temperatures make a gradual trend higher through the 70's for 
most of next week. Ensembles remain very dry for our area with the
next cold front hitting Washington state. About 2/50 12Z ECMWF 
ensembles bring some rain our way, so the chance of rain around 
Tuesday into Wednesday is very unlikely.

Heading towards the end of next week, there are more hints of a
trough passage and perhaps some rain here in southern Oregon and
northern California. Again, the odds remain very low and under 
5%.

Overall, active weather continues through the forecast period with
limited impacts to the public and regional infrastructure.

-Smith

MARINE...Updated 200 PM PDT Thursday, September 24, 2026... 
Southerly winds are present across area waters ahead of an 
approaching low pressure system. The system looks to swing to the 
north and keep the strongest winds out of this area, but gusty 
winds and very steep seas are still expected this evening into 
Friday morning. Gale gusts will be possible north of Reedsport late 
tonight through early Friday morning, while hazardous seas are 
expected in all other waters. Gale gusts leave the forecast but very 
steep and hazardous seas look to continue in all waters into Friday 
afternoon.

Winds and seas ease into Friday night but a thermal trough looks to 
develop on Saturday, which will keep some amount of unsettled seas 
across area waters. This through may be short-lived, with winds 
easing on Sunday. Long period westerly swell builds on Sunday 
afternoon, but right now guidance does not show this swell 
supporting Advisory conditions but local areas of steep seas may be 
possible. -TAD
